verdict.rationale: WooCommerce's Storefront theme documentation describes add_action() hooks that let developers insert HTML, PHP and JavaScript into its core templates. That is a documented, though thin, templating customization layer, and the Purple block theme adds customizable templates. Nothing in the evidence covers local theme preview or version-controlled theme deploys. Storybook (aimed at extension UX work) and the repo build setup are adjacent developer tooling, not storefront preview or deploy capabilities. Missing for 10: in-depth template override/templating docs, a local storefront preview workflow, version-controlled theme deploy tooling, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can customize storefront code with a documented templating layer, local preview, and version-controlled theme deploys

citations.quote: These allow you to insert sections of content using HTML, PHP, Javascript into its core templates.
WooCommerce introduces Purple, its first official block theme for beta testing, offering extensive customization options and modern templates for e-commerce.
